# Fig. 8 — The five-phase optimisation workflow

**Section 4.2** · how the 21-variable problem is decomposed.

**Status: `verified`.** A diagram. The phase sequence it shows is checked
against the driver below.

---

## This figure is not generated by the code

`optimization_workflow.pdf`, with a TikZ source alongside it. What is verifiable
is that the sequence it shows is the sequence the code runs.

## The two functional groups

| Group | Loops |
|---|---|
| **P-controllers** — active power and frequency | VSMP, RSCq, VDC, GSCq |
| **Q-controllers** — reactive power and AC voltage | VSMQ, RSCd, GSCd |

## The five phases

| Phase | Code | Optimises | Inherits from |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PDS | P-group frequency-domain specifications | CFRD baseline |
| 2 | QDS | Q-group frequency-domain specifications | Phase 1 |
| 3 | PCP | P-group 2-DOF setpoint weights | Phase 2 |
| 4 | QCP | Q-group 2-DOF setpoint weights | Phase 3 |
| 5 | VI | Virtual impedance | Phase 4 |

Each phase runs the GA on its own active subset with the rest held at the value
inherited from the preceding phase, and evaluates the same bi-objective fitness
under constraints C1–C3.

In `CONFIGURATION/CONFIG_POWER_SYSTEM.m`:

```matlab
RUN_MODE     = 3;
OPT_SEQUENCE = [1];  INIT_STEP = 0;   % Phase 1, from the CFRD baseline
OPT_SEQUENCE = [2];  INIT_STEP = 1;   % Phase 2, from the PDS result
...
OPT_SEQUENCE = [1 2 3 4 5];           % all five; 21.5 h measured
```

## The step the diagram omits, and the paper says so

**Extraction of a single design from the Pareto front returned by each phase.**
Each phase returns a front, not a design; the compromise solution is selected by
normalised compromise programming, described in Section 4.1.5. The figure must
be read together with that description and not as the complete procedure.

## That selection step never actually arbitrates

On this plant the front returned by every phase is a **single point** in
objective space. The compromise rule always has one candidate to choose from and
no trade-off between `J1` and `J2` is ever exposed.

The bi-objective formulation is nevertheless retained, and the reason is worth
carrying: **whether two objectives conflict is a property of the plant and the
operating point, and is not knowable before the search is run.** A scalarised
formulation — a single objective with weights fixed in advance — would have
returned the same design without ever disclosing that the weighting was
immaterial. The bi-objective form returned that information.

So if you reproduce a phase and get a single-point front, that is the expected
result, not a solver failure.

## What each phase actually contributes

The distribution is extremely uneven and is the finding of Section 5.5:

```
Phases 1-2 alone:   -23.5 % in J1,  -34.8 % in J2
All five phases:    -23.6 %,        -35.0 %
```

More than 99 % of both reductions comes from the first two phases. Phases 3–5
account for about 1 h of the 21.5 h total.

Two of the later phases behave in ways that look like failures and are not:
Phase 4 returns a bit-identical spectrum because the reference it weights is
zero everywhere, and Phase 5 carries a decision variable the model never reads.
Both are documented in
[`tab08_phase_progression.md`](tab08_phase_progression.md).

## The constraints every phase is evaluated under

| | Constraint |
|---|---|
| **C1** | Per-band eigenvalue damping, `ζ_min,b(x) ≥ 0.99 ζ_min,b(baseline)` for LF, MF, HF, plus the rightmost real eigenvalue |
| **C2** | Dual-endpoint: C1 verified at `SCR ∈ {1, 3}`; the ITAE objectives evaluated only at the worst case, `SCR = 1` |
| **C3** | DC-link: a soft multiplicative penalty `p = 1 + 100(ρ−1)` if the peak `\|Δu_dc\|` exceeds the baseline in either of two scenarios |

**C3 makes any DC-link degradation prohibitively expensive.** A 1 % worsening
doubles both objectives, so the GA will never select such a candidate.

**The 0.99 in C1 is not slack.** It absorbs the micro-perturbation introduced by
the integer encode–decode of the decision variables. Remove it and the baseline
fails its own constraint on a rounding difference. See
[`tab04_optimization_bounds.md`](tab04_optimization_bounds.md).

## Solver

NSGA-II via MATLAB's `gamultiobj`, population 80, maximum 25 generations per
phase — an upper bound of 2000 fitness evaluations per phase-run, and a cap
rather than a spend: Section 5.1 reports Phases 1 and 2 stopped by the
wall-clock limit before the generation count was reached.
